title: What did the server send?
fullTitle: The Browser Shows Your Page. What Does the Server Send?

captions.text: Two pages. Same article, headings, links, title.
In a browser you cannot tell them apart.
Raw HTML, before any script runs.
Generated page: 1 h1, 4 h2, 6 paragraphs, 3 links.
Client-rendered page: a shell and one script tag. 0 of 198 article words.
The script fetches /article.json and inserts the article.
With JavaScript on, both DOMs end with 6 paragraphs and 3 links.
JavaScript off: generated page still shows the article.
A browser with scripts off is not a Googlebot simulator. Google can run JS.
Generated response: text, headings and hrefs are already in the bytes.
No script, no hydration: the article has no client interactivity.
Crawl fetches. Render may run scripts. Index stores. Rank shows.
This test touches crawl and a slice of render; nothing more.
Static HTML guarantees neither indexing nor rankings.
Initial HTML and the eventual DOM are different artifacts.
Inspect both, and know which one you are looking at.
